title: Prompt, Fab, Flex: Agentic LLMs for Flexible Electronics Design
problem: Flexible electronics EDA workflows are complex, time-intensive, and inaccessible to non-experts. Existing LLM-driven design automation targets only conventional silicon, not flexible electronics with unique constraints.
motivation: Lower barriers to adoption and accelerate development of personalized, application-specific flexible electronics for extreme edge applications.
method: The framework uses a large language model—an AI trained on text—to automatically design circuits for flexible electronics, which bend and flex unlike rigid silicon. It automates the design workflow: writing hardware descriptions (RTL), converting them to working circuits (logic synthesis), and exploring different design options to optimize power consumption, speed, and chip size for machine learning classifier applications while respecting flexible materials' physical constraints. The system handles these trade-offs end-to-end without human intervention at each design step.
key_novelty: It's the first system using large language models to automate circuit design specifically for flexible electronics, which have different constraints than rigid silicon.
contributions: LLM-driven RTL generation for flexible electronics ML classifiers
Cross-layer PPA design space exploration for FE-based systems
Reduced barriers to adoption through automated hardware design methodology
limitations: Evaluation limited to ML classifier designs; generalization to complex digital systems unknown.
